title: Tad Jones introduces the evening and Earl King's biography
summary: Jones shows an English magazine covering New Orleans R&B and reads a formal introduction to Earl King: born 1934, Irish Channel, songs and artists who recorded them.

I've sort of formally written something out to introduce Earl King. He was born in New Orleans on February 7, 1934, the only child of Earl Johnson and Ernestine Hampton. He was raised in the Irish Channel and educated in the city's public school system, graduating from Booker T. Washington High School. He began his professional career in 1953 as a vocalist and a guitarist. Over the last 27 years, Mr. King has popularized such songs as those Logan Lowy Nights, Come On, Let the Good Times Roll, Trick Bag, Big Chief, and Let's Make a Better World. As a composer, his songs have been recorded by artists such as Dr. John, Fats Domino, Dusty Springfield, Dixie Cups, Jimi Hendrix, Lee Dorsey, Professor Longhair, and many others. In 1968, he was honored with the admission to the prestigious Who's Who in the South and Southwest.
